why: A byte order mark is legitimate once, at byte 0, and nowhere else. Measured: TextDecoder with its default ignoreBOM:false silently removes a second one, so a decoder that strips "the BOM" twice hides a U+FEFF from the rule. The fail side is docs/notes.md starting with two UTF-8 BOMs; the pass side starts with one. Let the decoder eat the second mark and the fail side goes green; treat the first one as a finding and the pass side goes red.
